Photo by Miguel MEDINA / AFP via Getty Images. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed and seven were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. Two bodies were also recovered from under the rubble, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,098 killed, with 173,571 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,072 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,463, while 799 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Hamas 's Gaza government announces dissolution: Gaza's Government Media Office announced Monday that its Emergency Committee has been dissolved, saying the move is intended to facilitate the transfer of administrative authority to the Palestinian-led National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) under Trump's Board of "Peace." The office said it had received "full assurance" that preparations for the handover had been completed and formally presented to Palestinian factions, clan leaders, and a United Nations observer. It added that only technical and professional staff would remain in their posts to prevent "an administrative and technical vacuum," while stressing that all public employees are "fully prepared to work" under the NCAG. The statement concluded by urging all relevant parties to "expedite the immediate entry" of the committee so it can assume its responsibilities. Hamas 's statement: Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem said that "a new positive step today to remove the occupation's pretexts" was taken today, following the announcement. Hamas has repeatedly stated its willingness to hand over governance to the NCAG since signing the October 2025 agreement. BoP 's response: The "Board of Peace" said it has "taken note" of the announcement, stressing that its assessment "will be guided by actions, not promises." In a on X, the Board said any transition must be "comprehensive" and comply with the Roadmap's requirements for governance, security, and political transition. It reiterated that the guiding principle remains "one authority, one law and one weapon," adding that "all weapons" must be consolidated under the control of the NCAG. Israel and Trump's Board have made the entry of the NCAG contingent on Palestinian acceptance of a 15-point "roadmap" that appears aimed at disarming the Palestinian resistance and the abandoning of the struggle for Palestinian national liberation. Read Drop's Site report on negotiations between the Board and Palestinians . Six killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza: At least six Palestinians were in Israeli air strikes on Gaza City and Khan Younis on Monday morning, according to WAFA. Two people were killed after an Israeli warplane struck an apartment in the Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood, southwest of Gaza City. In a separate attack, an Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, killing two and wounding at least 15 others. Two people were also killed in an Israeli strike on a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Al-Mawasi area of the southern Gaza Strip. Civil Defense teams also recovered the remains of eight Palestinians from beneath the rubble of a home in the Sabra neighborhood, south of Gaza City, which had been destroyed in an earlier Israeli air strike. At least 9,500 bodies remain buried under the rubble in Gaza, according to Palestinian estimates. Life of imprisoned Palestinian physician is in danger, report says: Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya's life is in immediate danger, Physicians for Human Rights Israel and his lawyer Saturday, after a prison visit. The director of Kamal Adwan Hospital had fresh, severe injuries to his head, eyes, ears, and neck, they said, leaving him so disfigured his own attorney initially struggled to recognize him. Attorney Nasser Odeh, who saw Abu Safiya Thursday at the underground Rakefet interrogation facility in Nitzan Prison, said he arrived shackled hand and foot, escorted by masked guards, struggling to breathe and speak, unable to sit upright, and repeatedly on the verge of losing consciousness. Abu Safiya told him that after his Supreme Court appeal was heard June 10, four or five guards entered his solitary cell at Ganot Prison and beat him with a hammer and batons, and that since his June 24 transfer to Rakefet he has been beaten daily, losing consciousness several times and receiving no medical treatment. "This is the last time you will see me," he told his lawyer. "They brought me here to kill me. I don't see myself surviving. This is the end." He has been held without charge since December 27, 2024. Dr. Abu Safiya's son described the visit in an Instagram post, available . Following an April petition by PHRI and Dr. Abu Safiya's lawyer, Israel's Supreme Court on Sunday ordered the state to respond by Tuesday, July 7, to a petition seeking the release of 14 Palestinian doctors detained without charge, and to specifically address the charges made about Dr. Abu Safiya's condition. Israeli attacks kill at least five Palestinians in Gaza over the weekend: An Israeli strike on a group of civilians at a water desalination plant east of Gaza City two on Sunday, according to WAFA. Another man died on Sunday, following an Israeli artillery attack east of al-Masdar. Israeli forces also at the tents of displaced people on the outskirts of Rafah, demolished residential buildings in northwestern Gaza, and fired upon fisherman's boats off the coasts of Rafah and Khan Younis. An Israeli drone strike a Palestinian man in Gaza City on Saturday evening, and wounded several others, Palestine Online reported. Also on Saturday, an Israeli strike near the Jabalia refugee camp another Palestinian man and wounded four others, in an attack that caused severe injuries to several, including a very young child. Israeli restrictions on crossings continue to suffocate Gaza: Five trucks of cooking gas entered the Strip, the Gaza Petroleum Authority reported on Sunday, reaching about 11,829 gas suppliers across Gaza. Under the terms of the ceasefire, at least 50 trucks of fuel are supposed to enter the Strip every day. Only 14.9% of the agreed-upon fuel has been allowed to enter Gaza, according to Palestinian figures obtained by Drop Site. On Sunday, it was that Israeli authorities would be moving the inspection center for Palestinians returning to Gaza from the area near the Rafah crossing to the Kerem Shalom crossing, according to Kan, Israel's public broadcaster. The change--justified by Israel by pointing to increased "smuggling" operations--will further limit evacuations, which have already been heavily curtailed by Israel since October of 2023. Israel has only allowed about a third of agreed crossings since it re-opened Rafah. Israeli attacks on West Bank escalate: On Sunday evening, Israeli forces shot and a 16-year-old in the Qalandia refugee camp, near Jerusalem, the Palestinian Health Ministry reported. A four-month-old Palestinian infant on Sunday after Israeli soldiers blocked his urgent medical transfer at the military checkpoint around his village of Deir Ammar, west of Ramallah, according to Ramallah Governor Laila Ghannam. Ghannam called his death "a stain on the conscience of humanity." More than 100 Israeli settlers reportedly and burned a cafe opposite Al-Zaytouna University in the Wadi al-Sha'ir area of Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus. Additional settler attacks were reported in Khirbet al-Kharaba south of Hebron, where homes came under attack; in the al-Ka'abneh community east of Jerusalem, where livestock were released among Palestinian homes; and in Masafer Yatta, where settlers reportedly stormed a home and tampered with its electricity. In an Instagram post on Monday, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich his plan for a "revolution in settlement," which would not only include the West Bank, but would extend into the Negev and the Galilee. His announcement follows last week's approvals of 13 new settlements by the Knesset. Israeli forces, settlers carried out over 11,000 attacks in occupied West Bank in the first half of 2026: Israeli forces and settlers 11,074 attacks against Palestinians and their property across the occupied West Bank during the first half of 2026, according to the Palestinian Commission Against the Wall and Settlements. Commission head Moayad Shaaban said the attacks included land seizures, settlement expansion, forced displacement, extrajudicial killings, land bulldozing, tree uprooting, property destruction, and movement restrictions through road closures and military checkpoints. He said 3,488 of the attacks were carried out by Israeli settlers, who killed a total of 17 Palestinians. Israeli authorities also approved the construction of 7,963 settlement units in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem in the first half of the year. Iran and Ceasefire Iranians gather to mourn late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians a funeral procession in Tehran for Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of Iran murdered by a U.S.-Israeli airstrike on the first day of the war, February 28. The six-day funeral ceremony will travel from Tehran, to the Iranian holy city of Qom, the Shia holy cities of Najaf and Karbala in Iraq, and Khamenei's hometown of Mashhad, where he will be buried on Thursday. Khamenei will be interred alongside several family members killed in the February strike, including his 14-month-old granddaughter, eldest daughter, son-in-law, and the wife of his son Mojtaba, Iran's new Supreme Leader. Mojtaba, the Supreme Leader's successor, is not expected to appear publicly; three of Khamenei's other sons attended the funeral prayers, according to the Associated Press. Mourners revenge for Khamenei's killing, carrying placards with images of U.S. President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, according to Al Jazeera. President Trump Axios on Saturday that negotiations between the U.S. and Iran would be paused until the funeral ceremonies conclude on Thursday, saying both sides agreed to "take a week off" and that "neither side will shoot at the other" during that time. Nonetheless, he appeared to threaten mourners by saying, about the Iranian leadership structure, "They are all there." "One shot [and we can take them all out]," he said, before saying that he had decided against such a course of action "because then we would have nobody to negotiate with." Israel 's Defense Minister: "Any Iranian leader" threatening Israel will "also be thwarted": Israel Katz on Monday that any future Iranian leader who seeks to destroy Israel "will also be thwarted," claiming that Iran's former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was "assassinated by Israel because he set in motion and led the plan to destroy Israel," the Times of Israel reported. Netanyahu could visit White House as early as this week: Trump Axios on Saturday that Netanyahu could visit the White House as early as this week, though Trump is expected to be in Turkey for the NATO summit on July 7-8. Iranian officials meet with Yemeni, Lebanese, and Palestinian counterparts: Amid the funeral ceremonies for Khamenei, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf held meetings with representatives for Hamas, Yemen's Ansarallah, Hezbollah, and the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. Describing his Sunday meeting with Hamas political chair Mohammed Darwish, Ghalibaf said that Iran was "not at peace with the United States," nor with Israel, and that, following the Supreme Leader, the government would continue to support "Muslims and the Resistance Front." "That support may take the form of missiles when necessary," he said, "and if political pressure is needed, then pressure will be applied through negotiations." Osama Hamdan, a member of Hamas's political bureau, also Khamenei by noting that the group had maintained a close relationship with the Supreme Leader for 34 years, and commended him for his "principled commitment" in support of the Palestinian cause. In an interview with al Alam during the funeral procession on Sunday, Hamdan said Khamenei had provided support for resistance groups while allowing them to make their own military and political decisions. Ship attacked off the coast of Yemen: A cargo vessel a distress alert after coming under attack about 30 nautical miles southwest of Al Hudaydah, Yemen, the UKMTO reported on Sunday. The vessel was reportedly approached by a small, unknown skiff carrying armed men, who opened fire. The ship's armed security team returned fire, and the attackers withdrew to a larger "mother ship" about 2 nautical miles away with its tracking system switched off. No injuries were reported and the vessel continued safely. No group claimed responsibility for the attack. The incident took place near Ansarallah-controlled territory, but the group did not immediately publicly issue a statement on the incident. U.S. Navy suspends search for missing sailor: The U.S. Navy on Sunday that it had suspended its search for a sailor who went missing in a helicopter crash in the Arabian Sea last week. Three of the MH-60 Sea Hawk's crew members were rescued and in stable condition. The Navy also indicated that there was no evidence that suggested the helicopter crash was a result of hostile action. The cause of the crash remains under investigation. Strait of Hormuz updates: The number of traceable daily transits through the Strait has more than , the Financial Times reported this weekend, rising from 1-2 per day for most of the war, to 8 per day on July 1. Roughly 125-140 transited per day before the war. Crude oil shipments have recovered to about 7 million barrels per day, up from near-zero levels during the height of the conflict, according to Citibank analysts by the Financial Times. Before the war, the strait carried roughly 15 million barrels of crude oil daily. Citibank said the 7 million barrels/day estimate likely understates actual traffic because many commercial tankers have switched off their public transponders for security reasons. At least 8 ships attempting to exit the Gulf along the Omani coast between Friday and Saturday, Bloomberg reported on Saturday, with some completing transit only after diverting to Iran's designated northern route. Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, Iran's ambassador to China, on Sunday that Tehran plans to introduce new service fees for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz once the current 60-day fee-free period expires, but would offer "special treatment" to countries it considers friendly. Iran responds to joint UK-French statement: After France and the United Kingdom intimated that they would use military force to work with Oman to secure Omani territorial waters in the vital Strait of Hormuz, Iran's deputy Foreign Minister Kareem Gharibabadi with a "serious warning," saying that the "security of Hormuz" lies with Iran and Oman alone and that "the crisis-makers" would be held responsible for "the consequences of their adventurism." Report: U.S. special operations task force remained on standby for possible Iran uranium recovery mission: A U.S. Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) task force has reportedly more than three months deployed in the Middle East preparing for a potential mission to recover highly enriched uranium from underground facilities in Iran, according to The High Side. The report said the operation would have involved transporting the recovered uranium to a laboratory in Hanford, Washington. Planning reportedly relied in part on Israeli intelligence to identify the locations of the uranium. According to the report, some officials believed the mission could cost an entire JSOC squadron of 60 to 90 operators. By late June, however, the mission was viewed as increasingly unlikely, with one former defense contractor saying the deployment had become more of "a deterrent to force a diplomatic solution" than a practical military option. Although most of the task force reportedly remains in the Persian Gulf region, a special operations official said that personnel are gradually returning to the United States. Lebanon Israeli military continues its attacks in Lebanon on Monday, despite "ceasefire": An Israeli airstrike on a Jeep in Nabatieh Al-Fawqah four people on Monday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency, including one elementary school principal, her mother, and two foreign workers. Israeli forces several homes in Aitaroun on Monday morning, after demolishing other structures in Houla overnight, the NNA reported. Israel's operations in the country continue despite a U.S.-backed framework deal, which was signed by the Israeli and Lebanese governments last week, and despite the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, whose first clause calls for an end to hostilities "on all fronts, including in Lebanon." Israeli attacks on Lebanon continued throughout the weekend: Israeli attacks killed one person and wounded another from Saturday to Sunday, the Lebanese Health Ministry reported, bringing the toll since March 2 to 4,304 killed and 12,203 wounded. An Israeli Apache Helicopter fired on Majdal Zoun on Saturday evening, killing a man who it claimed was armed, according to a statement from the Israeli military. Local journalists reported Israeli shelling in the municipalities of Deir Serian, Qantara, and Braasheet, and Mount Basil in Bint Jbeil, machine gun fire and explosions in Beit Yahoun, and a stun grenade dropped near Aita Al-Shaab. Israeli forces also large-scale demolitions in the Bint Jbeil district towns of Beit Yahoun and Kounin on Sunday, according to the NNA. Eyal Zamir, the IDF's chief of staff, visited the occupied Beaufort (Shiqif) Fortress on Sunday, saying the Lebanese Army must remove Hezbollah fighters from the area under the ceasefire framework. Israeli forces would continue operating from Lebanese territory, he said, prepared to launch new military operations if the ceasefire is violated. Netanyahu claims Lebanese Christians have asked Israel to annex their villages, dismisses rumors of Trump split: In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Netanyahu discussed his country's ongoing attacks. Netanyahu that Israel "take[s] care of its friends, especially the Christians in the Middle East," and alleged that village leaders had asked to be "annexed to Israel." Netanyahu considers limited withdrawal in Sunday meeting: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a high-level security meeting on Sunday to approve a pilot withdrawal from two villages in southern Lebanon under the U.S.-mediated framework, according to Israel's Channel 13. The withdrawal would reportedly be phased, with an initial "gradual" reduction of the Israeli military's presence, and Israeli officials have reiterated that redeployment depends on the Lebanese Army taking control of the areas. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Drop Site Exclusive: Internal poll finds Mallory McMorrow supporters lean toward Addul El-Sayed, giving potential boost after McMorrow quits race for U.S. Senate seat: Democratic Michigan state senatorMcMorrow her campaign to represent the state in the U.S. Senate on Sunday. Her exit clears the way for a head-to-head matchup in the August 4 Democratic primary between progressive Abdul El-Sayed , a physician and former Wayne County Health Director, and Rep. Haley Stevens , who has received millions of dollars from pro-Israel groups and has run to the right of both of her primary opponents. McMorrow had secured endorsements from Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.). With her exit, attention now turns to whether either senator will endorse El-Sayed or Stevens in the final month of the primary. An internal poll from Tulchin Research, conducted in late June for a pro-Abdul organization, Fighting for Michigan PAC, found 47% of McMorrow's supporters picked El-Sayed as their second choice, with 42% moving toward Stevens. That finding cuts against the conventional wisdom that Stevens would be the beneficiary of McMorrow's departure. The poll's overall finding--putting El-Sayed in front by 19 points--was a generous outlier toward El-Sayed, so caution is warranted, but the survey does complicate the picture. AOC meets with NYC primary winners: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez met with Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier, two of three Mamdani-endorsed candidates who won major victories in last month's New York primaries for dinner at a Himalayan restaurant in Jackson Heights on Sunday. Ocasio-Cortez did not either of the two DSA members, though she has defended both forcefully since, telling party colleagues attacking Avila Chevalier's old social media posts: "If you are already panicking and sending little messages in your group chats about how these people need to be reined in and tamped down and shown their place, you are creating the antagonistic dynamic that we do not need." McGovern promises votes on Israel, Gaza, and Humanitarian Aid: Rep. Jim McGovern (D-Mass.) Al Jazeera that if Democrats retake the House, he will become chair of the Rules Committee and would ensure votes and debates take place on Israel, Gaza, and humanitarian aid. Describing the Committee as the "traffic cop of Congress," McGovern blamed Republicans for "routinely" blocking amendments on humanitarian aid, Gaza, and the occupied West Bank from being considered. "I can at least guarantee that we're going to have votes on these matters," he said, telling Al Jazeera that he did not "come to Congress to just be window dressing." McGovern the Trump administration and his congressional colleagues for failing to ensure the entry of vital aid into Gaza, including minimum levels of food, water, medicine, and medical equipment, describing the administration's "indifference toward the suffering" of Palestinians in Gaza as "stunning," and characterizing this failure as "war crimes." Democratic Socialist of America has more than 120,000 members: The DSA on Saturday that their membership passed 120,000. With this, the group became the largest socialist organization in U.S. history, surpassing the 19th century Socialist Party of America, which was led by Eugene Debs. (One caveat: The U.S. population is three times bigger today than it was in the 1920s.) Internal Poll finds populist Will Lawrence the only Dem beating Republican Rep. Tom Barrett: A new poll sponsored by the Lawrence campaign, and conducted by Data For Progress, finds Sunrise co-founder Will Lawrence ahead of Barrett 48-46%, with his two corporate Democratic opponents behind by 1 point. The poll finds Lawrence with a commanding 19-point lead among independents, as he has leaned into his opposition to data center construction and condemned U.S. support for Israel's genocide in Gaza and the war on Iran. Lawrence appeared on Breaking Points Friday. The survey was first reported by Semafor. Trump pressures FIFA to remove red card on U.S. star: FIFA the suspension of Folarin Balogun , the U.S. team's top scorer, after President Trump reportedly called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the U.S. match on Wednesday to ask him to review the ruling, the NYT reported on Sunday, making Balogun eligible to play against Belgium on Monday. The move is extremely rare; according to the Times, it is the first reversal of a disqualifying decision in the World Cup since 1962. Belgium has appealed the decision. The Times also reported that commerce secretary Howard Lutnick , and White House task force head Andrew Giuliani put together a team of elite lawyers--from outside the government and against FIFA rules--to challenge the Balogun red card. House speaker plans reconciliation push for voter ID bill after floor revolt : House Speaker Mike Johnson he intends to move the SAVE America Act through budget reconciliation once the House returns from its July Fourth recess, after a group of conservative Republicans led byRep. Anna Paulina Luna blocked a procedural vote last week to protest the bill's stalled progress. Trump renewed his push for the legislation in a Saturday night speech on the National Mall, and Johnson said he plans to tie the bill to the defense authorization package to pressure the Senate, despite Senate Majority Leader John Thune 's warnings that doing so could jeopardize that must-pass legislation. Rubio tells U.S. embassies to lobby against Cuba resolution at the UN: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly U.S. embassies to lobby countries to oppose a July 7 U.N. General Assembly debate on the humanitarian impact of U.S. sanctions on Cuba, according to The Nation, citing a leaked State Department cable obtained by reporter Ken Klippenstein. The cable reportedly directed embassies to pressure their host nations, if they are strong U.S. allies, to criticize Cuba, to encourage nonaligned states to stay silent, and to warn countries supporting the debate that Washington "will be listening very closely" to their remarks. Other International News Drone strike kills 18 civilians in DRC: A drone strike allegedly conducted by the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group killed at least 18 civilians in the Congolese village of Mulima on Friday, local officials said. A regional administrator said health facilities, schools, and livestock were destroyed in several villages, driving a new wave of displacement. Officials blamed M23 and its allies and condemned repeated Rwandan violations of Congolese airspace. The killings come more than a year after Trump brokered a U.S. peace deal between Congo and Rwanda, one that also handed American firms preferential access to the region's cobalt, lithium, and coltan. Ansarallah attack kills 16 Yemeni soldiers: An Ansarallah assault on Saturday 16 soldiers of Yemen's Saudi-backed government and wounded 23 near the Red Sea city of Hodeidah, a government military official told AFP, in one of the deadliest clashes between the two sides in years. An officer said Ansarallah fighters briefly seized government positions using snipers, drones, and mortars before a counterattack retook them. On Sunday, a representative from the Ansarallah Foreign Ministry that the group would continue to try to break the Saudi-led blockade of the territory under the group's control, and to this effect would reopen the Sana'a International airport, "without asking for anyone's permission." Days earlier, Ansarallah repelled Saudi warplanes trying to prevent an Iranian civilian flight from landing in Sana'a. Though a de facto ceasefire has largely held since 2022, the Saudi-American blockade has never been lifted, creating a humanitarian catastrophe the UN has called one of the world's worst. Armed groups strike five locations across Mali as army claims control restored: Armed fighters five locations across Mali on Saturday, including the northern towns of Aguelhok, Anefis, and Gao, the central town of Sevare, and Kenieroba in the south, according to the AFP. The army reported that 20 fighters were killed in Sevare and six in Gao, and said the situation was "totally under control." The Azawad Liberation Front confirmed it had attacked Anefis in the Kidal region, where government and Russian forces are based following the ALF's earlier seizure of the town of Kidal in April. OPEC+ agrees to increase oil production: OPEC+, an alliance of the 12-member OPEC oil group and 10 partner producers led by Russia, agreed on Sunday to increase oil production by another 188,000 barrels per day starting in August. The move continues its gradual rollback of voluntary output cuts and marks the fifth straight monthly production increase. The decision comes partly in response to continued uncertainty over the status of the Strait of Hormuz and efforts by OPEC+ to calm global oil markets by increasing total supply. RSF attacks displace thousands in North Darfur villages near Tine : The Rapid Support Forces ethnically motivated attacks on six villages near Tine in North Darfur state starting last Wednesday, killing several civilians, injuring dozens, and forcing thousands to flee into neighboring Chad, according to Sudan Tribune. The attacks on the villages in the region which are home to the Zaghawa ethnic group follow recent gains by the Joint Force, an alliance backing the Sudanese army, which seized land in the area from the RSF. Separately, the cholera outbreak in Sudan's Kordofan region has reportedly , with hundreds of new infections registered. "The health system is unable to limit the spread of the disease due to deteriorated sanitation, contaminated water sources, damaged sewage networks, and a severe scarcity of safe drinking water," a doctor told the Sudan Tribune. More on life in El-Obeid, which has been under siege for months, is available in the latest from Drop Site contributor Eisa Dafalla, available. Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least 18: Russia waves of missiles and drones at Ukraine early Monday, killing at least 18 people and wounding at least 60 in Kyiv and the surrounding region, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine's air force said all 29 ballistic missiles launched by Russia overnight struck their targets, a fact Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said highlighted the country's need for Patriot missile interceptors amid a global shortage of the technology, calling on the United States and European allies to bolster Ukraine's air defenses ahead of a NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, this week. Separately on Monday, the mayor of the Russian city of Yaroslav reported that an Ukrainian drone attack on his city wounded two people. A wave of Ukrainian drones also struck the Omsk oil refinery--Russia's largest refinery accounting for 10% of its total output--amid an escalating Ukrainian campaign targeting oil and gas infrastructure. Death toll from Venezuelan earthquakes rises to 3,342, more than 40,000 still missing: Venezuela's official death toll from the June 24 twin earthquakes has to 3,342, National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez announced on Saturday. The UN estimates between 41,000 and 50,000 people remain unaccounted for, and Venezuelan authorities say more than 16,740 have been injured, and another 16,000 have been displaced from their homes. With the 72-hour survival window long past, AFP reports that international rescue teams from the U.S. and across South America are beginning to wind down search-and-rescue operations in the country. Syria delays first session of new transitional parliament: Syrian authorities the inaugural session of the country's new transitional parliament, which had been scheduled for Monday, The New Arab Reported, though it did not specify a reason for the delay. President Ahmed al-Sharaa appointed 70 members of the 210-seat body this week, while the Druze-Majority Suweida province has yet to select its members following last year's sectarian violence there. China conducts first ballistic missile test in Pacific since 2024 : China test-fired a long-range ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine into the Pacific on Monday, sending a dummy warhead into what Beijing called a "designated area" in the first such test in two years. The test drew criticism from New Zealand, Australia, and Japan, with officials calling it destabilizing and part of China's accelerating military buildup in the region. subject: It’s my Bday. 56 years. 70 pounds lost. 1 Sen. seat to flip.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JAMIE DAVIS FOR U
body:
I have to tell you — I've never felt better in my life.
| | | | | [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001a54Huv6NO0jZ9jV53XvkoS0Sp1EAl23F8xXwo1o3RBhFFsAW3_C1b75Xj3NyIlR2m9Wnir_4rCmeTSTgOloQkF1gNt6Q-SR6GOlz1X-8nd25fcg5QEnBbLdVZ65H_JLwh_n4zWxq08iuvjKbY8Tbz13i8FGHr9duDMH3_sUrFe60uB5QsD9jODwCbADW5xBasb8YZmJ6ftapsJkAH07pWg==&c=-a3xuI5kOfZ0s4cFJ9jr68VLPCX71KMeXXBtQ43Zbz2sX7BcPkbJ_Q==&ch=oGHOoyNhDdSMO8NGmzBwV0N0ZqjlhmJGkjqzIaSw68UfntuubdpZng==)
---
Peter,
Today is my 56th birthday. And I have to tell you -- I've never felt better in my life.
A year ago, I weighed over 360 pounds.
In late June, somewhere between knocking doors in the Louisiana heat, crisscrossing this great state from Shreveport to New Orleans, and putting in the kind of miles on my feet that I used to put on my tractor -- I stepped on the scale at 290. That's more than 70 pounds gone, y'all.
My doctor is happy. My team is happy. And I won't lie to you -- I'm pretty happy too.
---
| [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001a54Huv6NO0jZ9jV53XvkoS0Sp1EAl23F8xXwo1o3RBhFFsAW3_C1b75Xj3NyIlR2m9Wnir_4rCmeTSTgOloQkF1gNt6Q-SR6GOlz1X-8nd25fcg5QEnBbLdVZ65H_JLwh_n4zWxq08iuvjKbY8Tbz13i8FGHr9duDMH3_sUrFe60uB5QsD9jODwCbADW5xBae3xXecRnb_eS9e3hKvLxuw==&c=-a3xuI5kOfZ0s4cFJ9jr68VLPCX71KMeXXBtQ43Zbz2sX7BcPkbJ_Q==&ch=oGHOoyNhDdSMO8NGmzBwV0N0ZqjlhmJGkjqzIaSw68UfntuubdpZng==)
---
But here's what's funny about this whole thing. When I decided to run for Senate, I didn't set out to get in shape. I set out to fight for Louisiana.
Every morning, I think about the people I met the day before. The farmer in northeast Louisiana who doesn't know how he'll make it through another season. The woman working two jobs who still can't afford her insulin. The young person who loves Louisiana but can't see a future here anymore.
My name is Jamie Davis, I'm the Democratic nominee for the US Senate in Louisiana. I'm 70 pounds lighter. I'm healthier than I've been in years. I won the runoff by a landslide. They are calling our campaign "the miracle on the Mississippi" and I wake up every single morning with a fire in my belly I haven't felt since I was a young man working alongside my father on our farm.
I'm not a man who asks for much on his birthday. But today I'm going to ask for one thing.

| | **China Has Mastered the Electric Stack. The US Is Framed as a Petrostate. This Structural Divergence Will Shape the AI Trade for the Next Decade — and It Is Already Visible in the Data.**
---
| | A geopolitical analysis published today describes the sharpest structural divergence of 2026: China has become what analysts call the world’s first **“electrostate”** — mastering EVs, batteries, drones, robotics, and AI infrastructure simultaneously. The United States is increasingly framed as the world’s largest petrostate, exporting 20th-century energy models while Beijing offers emerging markets 21st-century infrastructure at aggressively low prices. Confidence that the US will still lead the world by 2030 has fallen to just **37%** among international affairs analysts surveyed by the World Economic Forum, down from 70% a year ago. McKinsey’s 2026 global trade update found that AI-related hardware — semiconductors and data-processing equipment — grew nearly 40% in 2025, accounting for roughly a third of all global trade growth. China’s 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) explicitly targets semiconductor self-reliance. Emerging markets are already choosing between US AI infrastructure at premium prices and Chinese alternatives at subsidized ones.
---
| | For the American investor, the practical implication is not that Chinese competition makes US chip stocks worthless on any near-term horizon — it does not. **Micron’s $50B Q4 guidance, NVIDIA’s architecture dominance, and TSMC’s manufacturing lead remain intact.** The implication is that the AI trade’s long-term valuation case requires US semiconductor design and manufacturing superiority to hold through a period when China is explicitly and resourcefully trying to erode it. The CHIPS Act, TSMC Arizona, and advanced chip export controls are the policy instruments designed to maintain that gap. Whether they succeed is a 5–10 year question — not a 2026 question. In the near term, the AI trade is intact. But the structural headwind is real, and it is the reason the AI trade deserves a valuation premium only if the architecture lead is durable. **Size your conviction accordingly.**
---
| | Sources: WorldAtNet Geopolitics 2026, July 5, 2026 · McKinsey Global Trade Update, March 2026 · Lazard Geopolitical Trends 2026

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Can I share something personal with you?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
Hey, friend — it’s Deb. Can I tell you a bit about my story?

From my great-grandmother, mother, and many before them, I’m blessed to come from generations of Pueblo women who taught me what it means to be fierce and resilient.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk971-su-nd&t=1&akid=10748%2E400544%2EpJCt2y)
Some of my earliest memories are of watching my grandmother bake bread in her mud oven and stir huge pots of [**posole**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk971-su-nd&t=2&akid=10748%2E400544%2EpJCt2y). I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours. To this day, there’s nothing I enjoy more than making traditional New Mexican meals for my friends and family.
For me, cooking has always been a way to foster connection and build community, which is exactly what we’re doing now in this campaign. I’ve had the chance to sit down with New Mexicans in living rooms, at kitchen tables, in restaurants, parks — in all 33 counties — to hear about their lives, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Those conversations are a reminder of just how high the stakes are in this race and why I’m in it: **to fight for and deliver for New Mexicans.**
Friend, more and more, we are seeing extremism take place and a President who isn’t fighting for us. Democratic Governors — including this seat right here in New Mexico — are essential to serve as a backstop when the federal government abuses its resources and undermines civil liberties.
As Governor, I will fight to expand healthcare access, lower costs, build stronger schools, and invest in safer communities. Meanwhile, the Republicans in this race want to open New Mexico to Trump’s extremist agenda. **That’s why this race is so important.**
Fox News is calling New Mexico a top flip opportunity for Republicans. Now more than ever, the support of every single member of this team matters.
I feel so grateful for this grassroots community — including you, friend. [**Since you're a member of our team, I’d like to share my favorite New Mexican recipe, green chile chicken posole, with you today.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk971-su-nd&t=3&akid=10748%2E400544%2EpJCt2y)**** This recipe means a lot to my family, and I hope that you’ll enjoy it with your family, too.
| | [VIEW RECIPE >>>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk971-su-nd&t=4&akid=10748%2E400544%2EpJCt2y)
---
Friend, thank you for letting me take a moment of your time to share my story and why this campaign means so much to me. We’ve got a lot of work ahead, so fuel up with a pot of posole and get ready! With good food and good friends, we can do anything.
Be Fierce,
Deb
|

name: Dr. Annie Andrews
subject: I'm a doctor. I'm scared. And I'm running for Senate.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-andrews [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-andrews]
I'm a pediatrician. I’m pissed. I’m scared. And I need your help to defeat Lindsey Graham in the U.S. Senate.
I’m not the “monsters-under-the-bed” kind of scared. I’m the “I’ve watched children suffer from preventable illness and injury while politicians do absolutely nothing” kind of scared.
I’ve treated kids who’ve been shot. Kids whose families struggle to afford their medications.
Kids who live with mold that causes asthma attacks, miss school for climate disasters, and watch politicians use them as political pawns.
And now? Trump is causing chaos and Lindsey Graham is right by his side.
And Medicaid — the program that keeps half our pediatric patients insured, healthy, and...alive — is on the chopping block to pay for tax breaks for billionaires.
So yeah, I never planned to run for Senate.
But I’m scared. I’m pissed. I’m motivated. And I’m 100% in.
I’m running for Senate in South Carolina to defeat Lindsey Graham and to fight for the kids no one in D.C. seems to be thinking about. So I need you with me.
We need to hit 10,000 donations before July 15th to prove that this campaign can go the distance. Can I count on you to split a donation with my campaign and Equal Opportunity Now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-andrews]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT LINDSEY GRAHAM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-andrews]
I’m running because the Republican Party, led by people like Lindsey Graham, is dismantling the very systems that keep our kids safe here in South Carolina.
I’m running because the issues I care about — children’s healthcare, vaccines, gun violence, public education, Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare — are under direct attack right now.
And I’m running because I consider it my professional duty as a pediatrician — to give children a strong voice at the national level. Too many are comfortable on the sidelines. That won’t work for me.
We need bold leaders who aren’t afraid to fight. I am ready.
Even though the path will be hard, I know Lindsey Graham must be held accountable. He certainly doesn’t deserve a free pass back to D.C. for six more years.
That’s why I’m running for US Senate. To defeat Trump’s lapdog and fight for everyday Americans. But, I need your support today. Can you rush a split donation of $10 (or whatever you can spare) between Equal Opportunity Now and me to become a Founding Donor to my campaign? >> secure.actblue.com/flipSC [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-andrews]
Thank you for believing in this campaign,
Dr. Annie Andrews
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

---

| | A few weeks ago, we learned through news reports that the Trump administration was planning to dismantle the Ocean Observatories Initiative, a network of over 900 sensors on the ocean floor off the coasts of Oregon, Washington, Alaska, North Carolina, and Greenland. No warning, no scientific review, and no legal notification to Congress as required by law. This system has been tracking ocean circulation, marine ecosystems, extreme weather, and climate change for over a decade. Fishers check its real-time wind and wave data before heading out to sea. Meteorologists use it to improve hurricane and tsunami forecasts. Scientists have cited it in over 500 published studies. Congress funded it to run another 15 to 20 years. The administration wanted it gone by 2027, and they'd already started pulling buoys out of the water off Oregon's coast. **I wasn't going to let that happen, so I teamed up with Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and we led a bipartisan push to stop it. We introduced legislation to block further dismantling until a real scientific review could be conducted, and the Senate passed our measure by unanimous consent.** The very next day, because of our work and pressure from the public, the National Science Foundation reversed course. They announced they would pause all removal efforts immediately and convene an expert panel to determine the system's future. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134752183/632044646/-1030352903?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTMyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNWEyOTI2OS01Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=etpscm_vCe6914_-g3PnKlT8HXGwvMU5raibCaKaVXM=&emci=1bb70441-4c76-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=25a29269-5b79-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=7731215) Some sensors had already been pulled from the water off Oregon and Washington, but scientists at Oregon State are now working to get them redeployed. We'll be watching closely to make sure the administration follows through on its commitment to put them back. This is part of Trump's broader attack on science — gutting NOAA, hollowing out the EPA, walking away from climate science right when we need it most. Every one of those fights matters, and in this one, we showed that bipartisan pressure works. clean_body: A few weeks ago, we learned through news reports that the Trump administration was planning to dismantle the Ocean Observatories Initiative. | | | | A few weeks ago, we learned through news reports that the Trump administration was planning to dismantle the Ocean Observatories Initiative, a network of over 900 sensors on the ocean floor off the coasts of Oregon, Washington, Alaska, North Carolina, and Greenland. No warning, no scientific review, and no legal notification to Congress as required by law. This system has been tracking ocean circulation, marine ecosystems, extreme weather, and climate change for over a decade. Fishers check its real-time wind and wave data before heading out to sea. Meteorologists use it to improve hurricane and tsunami forecasts. Scientists have cited it in over 500 published studies. Congress funded it to run another 15 to 20 years. The administration wanted it gone by 2027, and they'd already started pulling buoys out of the water off Oregon's coast. I wasn't going to let that happen, so I teamed up with Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and we led a bipartisan push to stop it. We introduced legislation to block further dismantling until a real scientific review could be conducted, and the Senate passed our measure by unanimous consent. The very next day, because of our work and pressure from the public, the National Science Foundation reversed course. They announced they would pause all removal efforts immediately and convene an expert panel to determine the system's future. Some sensors had already been pulled from the water off Oregon and Washington, but scientists at Oregon State are now working to get them redeployed. We'll be watching closely to make sure the administration follows through on its commitment to put them back. This is part of Trump's broader attack on science — gutting NOAA, hollowing out the EPA, walking away from climate science right when we need it most. Every one of those fights matters, and in this one, we showed that bipartisan pressure works. Onward! It’s been one year since Donald Trump signed the GOP’s “Big Beautiful Bill,” and calling it disastrous would be an understatement.
This bill was historic for all the wrong reasons. It was the single largest transfer of wealth from the working class to the ultrawealthy in our nation’s history . It was the largest cut to food assistance in our nation’s history.
That is all in addition to increasing consumer energy costs, exploding the national debt, and more.
And as a doctor who had the honor of caring for patients for more than 20 years, I can tell you that the largest cut ever to Medicaid — which provides health insurance to 80 million Americans and covers almost half of all American children — will be devastating.
But one of the most chilling parts of this travesty was that the Republican majority simply didn’t care — and they literally told us so.
→ Vice President JD Vance called gutting Medicaid “minutiae” and kicking millions of Americans off their health insurance “immaterial.”
→ Republican Senator Mitch McConnell said Americans who are concerned about losing Medicaid will "get over it."
→ Republican Senator Joni Ernst defended the life-threatening gutting of Medicaid by saying, “Well, we are all going to die.”
All of it to make the math work so Republicans could give tax breaks to the wealthiest among us, while doing nothing to bring the cost of living down for Americans.
They didn’t care that families would lose their health care coverage, seek less care, or be unable to afford their medications.
It’s important to remember that it doesn’t matter if you have Medicaid or not — the Republicans’ cuts to health care hurt everyone. Because it doesn’t matter what insurance you have if your local hospital or clinic no longer exists.
It is unconscionable. Frankly, it’s immoral.
Since this legislation went into effect, the Republican majority has continued to cede more power to the President, doing his bidding without question or concern for the majority of American families who are hurting.
The only way to put an end to this cruel agenda and start making government deliver results that actually help Minnesotans and Americans is to take back the House this November and elect Democrats up and down the ticket.

Hey folks,
I hope you all had a great Fourth of July weekend and got a chance to spend some time with the people you love.
We recorded this conversation over the holiday weekend, but the issues we talked about haven't gone anywhere. We dug into why Republicans keep falling back on the same tired "communist" attacks, how those distractions help take attention away from corruption, and what it really means to fight for a country that works for everyone. This one gets personal, and I think it's just as relevant today as it was when we hit record.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:08**] We kick things off by talking about our Fourth of July plans, sharing a few stories from the holiday weekend, and reflecting on why meeting so many of you around the country keeps us motivated to keep doing this work.

body:
We did it. Because of you, we are headed to November.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/tessaforca/on-to-the-general-election-5864875?e=db7cb92046)
---
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/sylJ5DFRm0p?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c)
| |
# On to the General Election in November!
---
|
---
| | **A Note from Tessa Lynn Hodge**
We did it.Because of you, we are headed to November.To every person who donated, volunteered, knocked doors, made phone calls, sent a text, shared a social media post, put up a yard sign, or simply told a friend or family member about this campaign, thank you. This victory belongs to every single one of you.We didn't have the biggest machine. We didn't have unlimited money. What we had was people. People who believe our district deserves a representative who will fight for working families instead of special interests.And together, we earned our place in the general election against Jay Obernolte.Now the real fight begins.I'm not going to pretend the road ahead is easy. It isn't. We're taking on an incumbent with deep pockets and powerful allies. Every attack ad, every misleading mailer, and every attempt to convince voters that change is impossible is coming our way.But I've never backed down from a fight worth having.As a social worker, I've spent my career standing beside people during the hardest moments of their lives. I know what perseverance looks like. I know what resilience looks like. And I know what happens when ordinary people decide they've had enough and refuse to give up.That's exactly how we're going to win.This race is bigger than one congressional district. California has the opportunity to help determine the balance of power in Congress. At a time when voting rights have been weakened and districts across the country are becoming harder to compete in, every seat we flip matters. Every conversation matters. Every volunteer shift matters. Every dollar matters.We can flip this district, but only if every one of us shows up.I want to give a special thank you to my incredible team both past and present: Alex, Denise, Jack, Isaac, Jim, Stasik, Jay, and Stephanie. You've poured your hearts into this campaign, and I am endlessly grateful for your commitment, your sacrifice, and your belief in this movement.To my husband, Andrew, thank you for being my rock through every late night, every early morning, every setback, and every victory. You've believed in me from day one, and I couldn't ask for a better partner in this journey or in life.I also want to thank Alexis Claiborne, Paul Chakalian, Edwin Alonzo, Pat Wallis, and Karen Matthews. Running for office is never easy. It takes courage to put your name on the ballot and fight for what you believe in. While we were competitors during the primary, our shared goal remains the same: giving this district the representation it deserves. I appreciate the work each of them and their supporters put into this race, and I look forward to working together to flip this seat.Today we celebrate.Tomorrow we organize.We knock more doors.We make more calls.We register more voters.We tell our story in every corner of this district.We outwork the opposition.And in November, we make history.If you've been waiting for the moment to jump in, this is it.Let's build the campaign that nobody thought was possible.Let's shock the political establishment.Let's flip CA-23.Let's send a social worker to Congress.Let's win.
---
|
---
| | **Distinction Alert**
* Tessa was given the Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction

---
|
---
|
---
| | **Watch Party**

Thank you to everyone who joined us for our election night watch party!
---
|
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

**Primary Results**
“Hodge runs as the broad Democratic alternative, topping most groups Obernolte cedes: she leads among Asian (59%), Black (51%), Latino (43%), young, renter voters, and registered Democrats. Her coalition is notably more diverse than her 21.6% topline implies, suggesting she consolidated the anti-Obernolte vote across nearly every non-White, non-senior segment.” ~Summary from PDI (Political Data Intelligence)
---
|
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |

**Welcome to the team, Jim!**

Jim will be serving as our Redlands/Loma Linda field coordinator. He will be working to identify volunteers and community events for the campaign to attend, setting up canvassing opportunities, and more! If you are interested in becoming a field coordinator in your area, please email [info@tessaforca.com](mailto:info@tessaforca.com).

---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | **Please, help us get my Candidate Statement in the Voter Guide**

We have to raise another $15,000 for the Candidate statement in the voter guide for the general election. Altogether that means the campaign has to pay $30,000 to have candidate statements in the voter guides. This is further evidence of why, so often, only the wealthy are able to run for and win offices. We are not wealthy, so it is only because of the support of my community that we have made it this far.

subject: Proof that we can stop them

body:

Hi friends,
For once, we have some positive news out of the Supreme Court! Last week, the highest court in the country upheld birthright citizenship, ruling that Donald Trump’s horrific executive order attempting to strip it away is unconstitutional.
I want to take a moment to talk about what that actually means.
This is a win for the American people, for our democracy, and for our collective future. This win happened because people all across the country spoke out – loudly, angrily, and immediately after Trump signed the executive order on day one of his second term.
Democratic state attorneys general filed lawsuits. Courts all over the country blocked the order from going into effect.
Americans from all backgrounds called their members of Congress and demanded action to protect this fundamental right.
And ultimately, a class of children who would have been directly harmed by this order filed the lawsuit that went all the way to the Supreme Court. And now, the highest court in the land agreed: Trump went too far.
(You know this administration’s position is really extreme when even THIS Supreme Court says that.)
But here’s the bigger takeaway: this is what fighting back looks like. It’s messy and it takes time and there are no guarantees, but when we stay the course and keep showing up when it matters most, we can win.
Every lawsuit filed, every court that blocked this order, every person who refused to look away – that’s how we got here today. And the simple fact that this executive order never went into effect is a testament to the strength of our resolve and our belief in this fundamental right.
Look, I’m under no illusion that this administration has learned its lesson and dropped its assault on birthright citizenship – I mean, right after the ruling, Stephen Miller went on Fox News to talk about how the Trump administration is going to take “a hard look” at banning foreign pregnant women from the country.
And I definitely don’t believe we should restore much faith in the Supreme Court; after all, upholding an essential constitutional right like this one should be considered the bare minimum, not a rare victory for democracy. (And it should have been unanimous, not a 5-4 ruling.)
This administration will continue to attack our rights, Republicans in Congress will continue to bow down to Donald Trump, and the Supreme Court will continue to fail us. But this win is proof that we can stop them. In the courts, in Congress, and at the ballot box in November.
I will continue to do every single thing in my power to fight back against whatever illegal, cruel, and destructive thing this administration throws at us. Are you with me? If so, add your name to show your support and send a message that you’re still in this fight.
ADD MY NAME [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
I’m ready to keep this fight going, and I’m proud to have you by my side.
-Sara

Their door knockers are hitting their lists. _And if we are not doing the same thing -- right now -- we are falling behind._ **I know this because I've lived it.** In 2024, my team spent over a year embedded on the ground in Pennsylvania before Election Day. We helped register hundreds of thousands of new Republican voters. We chased down every outstanding mail-in ballot we legally could. We drove voters to the polls on Election Day. **That is why Pennsylvania went red.** Not because of any law. Not because of any court ruling. Peter,

With exactly one month until the Tennessee primary election, Justice
Democrat Justin J. Pearson is entering the final phase of this race with a
massive new endorsement: Senator Bernie Sanders!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260706-jp.KrTrno&refcode=em20260706-37994&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=37994%2E1203867%2E-rgwfn ]Tweet from @BernieSanders: "Justin understands the needs of Tennessee's
working class, and he knows that leaders who go to Washington must not
sell their souls to lobbyists and the corruption of our political system.
I am proud to endorse him for Congress."

Like Bernie, Justin believes that nobody should have to struggle to afford
healthcare or have their water, land, or air exploited for profit by the
biggest corporations in the richest country in the world. He supports
Medicare for All, environmental justice, affordable housing for all,
taxing the billionaires, and ending the genocide in Gaza.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260706-jp.KrTrno&refcode=em20260706-37994&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=37994%2E1203867%2E-rgwfn ]Bernie is standing with Justin in these final weeks — will you join
him, Peter?
Split a grassroots donation to Justin’s campaign and Justice Democrats now
to help us win →

Justin is running for Congress with the same fighting spirit that’s fueled
his entire career.

As a state representative and member of the Tennessee Three, Justin was
expelled by Republicans for joining protesters in demanding action on gun
violence. He’s also led the fight to stop trillionaire Elon Musk’s xAI
data center from poisoning and extorting the South Memphis community.

Like Bernie said, “As billionaires and Big Tech take more and more control
over our lives and our government, we need leaders like Justin J. Pearson
who have the experience and track record of standing up to the rich and
power-hungry elites.”

Justin was originally challenging Do-Nothing Democrat Rep. Steve Cohen for
this seat, but the incumbent dropped out after the Tennessee GOP
gerrymandered this district to dilute Black voting power and hurt
Democrats’ chances of ever winning in the general.

But Justin refuses to surrender our democracy to a handful of white
supremacists hell-bent on destroying it.

Now, Justin is the unexpected frontrunner in this primary. If he wins on
August 6th, he’ll face off against the state’s Republican machine intent
on delivering an all-GOP delegation for Donald Trump in November.

We need to come together in these last four weeks to make Justin the
official Democratic nominee for TN-09, and then fight like hell to defeat
his Republican opponent in November.

Like all Justice Democrats, Justin doesn’t take a dime from corporate
PACs. Instead, he’s relying on grassroots supporters like you to turn his
momentum into victory.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260706-jp.KrTrno&refcode=em20260706-37994&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1004&akid=37994%2E1203867%2E-rgwfn ]With this primary just one month from today, we need every resource
possible to reach voters, fight back against the Republican machine, and
send another Justice Democrat to Congress. Will you split
$10 or whatever you can between Justice Democrats and Justin
right now?

# [Trump rings opening bell from Oval Office to launch Trump Accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/56ea0c77-05a5-47f6-aa3b-77ed427f5b07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump **[rang the opening bell from the White House Oval Office](https://substack.com/redirect/cdd04b7a-851a-4cdf-a8d3-17a74082fcb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Monday with the NYSE and Nasdaq for the first joint market open there, promoting newly launched tax-advantaged Trump Accounts for children under 18.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56ea0c77-05a5-47f6-aa3b-77ed427f5b07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **High profile attendees:** Michael Dell and Susan Dell pledged over $6 billion while Brad Gerstner, Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeffrey Sprecher, Sen Ted Cruz, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and others joined the event.
* **Account structure:** Tax advantaged vehicles available to all Americans under age 18 with up to $5,000 annual contributions from parents, friends or employers and $1,000 government seed money for babies born from 2025 through 2028 invested in low cost ETFs.
* **Strong early results:** Six million families have opened accounts with 86 %rcent from households earning less than $200,000 as Bessent called it creating an ownership economy where citizens become shareholders.
* **Historic firsts:** Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev called the accounts potentially life changing while Gerstner said this makes real the promise of the American dream for everybody.

# [Lockheed Martin leads race for $3.5 billion Ultra Maritime buy](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lockheed Martin is l**[eading the race for a roughly $3.5 billion acquisition of naval defense firm Ultra Maritime](https://substack.com/redirect/a6b2f24b-8ab7-41ea-9676-2ffc53d0f2dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** specializing in anti submarine radar electronic warfare and torpedo defense technology.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal structure:** Ultra owned by private equity firm Advent International with Guggenheim and JPMorgan advising on the sell side and possible announcement as early as this week.
* **Company focus:** Ultra makes radar electronic warfare systems and torpedo defense countermeasures amid rising global demand for munitions.
* **Market backdrop:** Defense stocks have enjoyed a bumper year in 2026 as conflicts increase demand with global defense outlays climbing to $2.89 trillion in 2025 led by European spending.
* **Context note:** Advent reportedly put Ultra up for sale earlier in 2026 for more than $4 billion.

# [Electronic warfare boom sends defense stock valuations skyrocketing](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Analysts say investors must **[rethink defense stock valuations as winners increasingly resemble software](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad7f598-1895-421f-aa26-870dbe2b4fb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and AI companies driven by electronic warfare drones and AI enabled systems.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Strategic shift:** Panmure Liberum strategist Joachim Klement called electronic warfare a tech phenomenon requiring companies to be traded like tech firms deserving much higher valuations.
* **Investor behavior:** Recent weakness in European defense stocks reflects rotation into AI stocks and more selective buying weighing legacy platforms against AI drones and deep strike capabilities.
* **Legacy risks:** Germany cancellation of the F126 program shows big ticket conventional programs remain vulnerable while Leonardo and BAE Systems focus on AI enhanced drone systems.
* **Spending drivers:** European rearmament continues unabated especially in Germany and Poland despite fiscal pressure separating winners from conventional arms makers.

# [Anthropic lease triggers massive 16% explosion in TeraWulf shares](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic **[signed a 20 year lease for TeraWulf data center in Kentucky](https://substack.com/redirect/5e843132-a81b-46ce-803f-1c7f464a6f11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** offering around 400 megawatts with first power in the second half of 2027 expected to generate roughly $19 billion in revenue.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Strategic validation:** TeraWulf CEO Paul Prager said the deal with one of the world's leading AI companies validates the strategy and establishes a long duration revenue stream.
**Share reaction:** TeraWulf shares soared more than 16% in premarket trading and the stock is up more than 80% this year after pivoting from crypto mining.
**Additional move:** TeraWulf sold its 50% interest in a 168 megawatt data center in Abernathy Texas to an investor group led by Fluidstack.
**Facility details:** The Hawesville Kentucky site located about one hour southwest of Louisville will support AI infrastructure demands.

Dan Meuser and Gil Cisneros **[disclosed family purchases of SpaceX stock days after the June IPO](https://substack.com/redirect/addc35c9-8bfb-49f0-b6fe-d4d496df016e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that reached over $2 trillion market cap raising roughly $75 billion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Purchase details:** Meuser's dependent child bought between $15,001 and $50,000 on June 15 while Cisneros bought between $1,001 and $15,000 on June 18 with no evidence of nonpublic information use.
* **Committee sensitivity:** Meuser sits on House Financial Services while Cisneros sits on House Armed Services overseeing the Defense Department a major SpaceX customer.
* **Cisneros statement:** He said his wife and he use outside fiduciary advisors who manage a diverse portfolio and he has always complied with all stock trading rules.
* **Broader context:** SpaceX shares closed at $162 Thursday up 8% from $150 opening but 20% below June 16 high with more disclosures expected.

# [Major setback: Nvidia "Kyber" AI chip racks slammed back to 2028](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's next generation Kyber NVL144 rack architecture for Rubin Ultra chips **[has been delayed more than 12 months to 2028](https://substack.com/redirect/0988c161-43eb-4af2-ac56-77cd21c7d5fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** due to difficulties manufacturing the key PCB midplane circuit board.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b677760-be2b-4aa7-838e-2b25b7489275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **System purpose:** Kyber packs 144 powerful chips into a single cabinet using vertical compute trays to boost density and reduce latency for training advanced AI models.
* **Additional impact:** Larger NVL576 system linking eight racks is also likely delayed or limited to small volumes while backup plan to bolt two racks together was scrapped after customer pushback.
* **Roadmap strain:** The setback adds to concerns that Nvidia's annual release cadence collides with manufacturing limits potentially opening technical opportunity for AMD and Google chips.
* **Current status:** Rubin systems remain in full production shipping this fall to eight cloud partners including Amazon Microsoft and Google with data center revenue projected 20% above consensus.

* **Market importance:** India holds the largest user base for Instagram with over 480 million users and more than 400 million Facebook users plus over half a billion on WhatsApp.
* **Meta response:** The company maintains zero tolerance policy for child abuse content and uses AI to detect violations but battles criminals among its 3.5 billion users globally.

| I want to tell you exactly why this race deserves your support. No fluff. Just the facts.

**1️⃣****This seat decides the House majority.** Democrats cannot take back the House without holding NY-04. It is that simple and Republicans know it which is why they have made this district a top priority.

**2️⃣****I have a record of getting things done.** I managed a nearly $500 million budget as Hempstead Town Supervisor, took on corruption and lowered taxes in a town that had not elected a Democrat in over a century. I brought that same fight to Congress and I’m not stopping now.

**3️⃣****My opponent has shown you exactly who she is.** She went on television and said she supports Trump's harmful agenda and his bill that guts Medicaid and slashes food assistance. She’s not running to represent NY-04. She’s running to be a rubber stamp for Trump in Washington.

On July 6th, 1863, a liberal arts professor named Joshua Chamberlain was doing a bit of writing.
#
On July 6th, 1863, a liberal arts professor named Joshua Chamberlain was doing a bit of writing.
Three days earlier, he had defended a rocky hill outside of Gettysburg, Pennsylvania from advancing Confederate infantry. The hill has come to be known as Little Round Top. It was the extreme left flank of the Army of the Potomac, and Chamberlain’s 20th Maine had been ordered to hold it at any cost.
If Little Round Top fell, if Chamberlain’s 20th Maine was forced from the summit, the entire Union line would be vulnerable to Confederate artillery fire, assault, and envelopment. The Confederacy had momentum, morale was high — this was the farthest they had advanced into Union territory.
Joshua Chamberlain, 34 years old, a professor of rhetoric and oratory, understood the stakes. The 20th Maine was pressed repeatedly, taking heavy casualties, exhausting their ammunition. And at the breaking point, when many others may have chosen withdrawal or surrender, Chamberlain ordered a bayonet charge. The 20th Maine not only held Little Round Top — they drove the Confederates from the slopes.
Little Round Top changed the direction of the battle of Gettysburg, the Civil War, and the future of the United States of America. And on July 6th, 1863, Chamberlain wasn’t resting. He was writing his after action report and chasing the Army of Northern Virginia as they retreated through Maryland. He was awarded the Medal of Honor, and the professor became known as “The Lion of Little Roundtop.”
The war didn’t end for another two years, but when it did, Chamberlain himself presided over the formal surrender of the Confederate Army at Appomattox Court House. Two years later, he was elected Governor of Maine.
VoteVets exists to find the Chamberlains, people willing to put themselves in harm’s way and hold the line. To fight Little Round Tops, to advance where others won’t and win where others can’t. To turn Veterans into Councilmembers, Representatives, Governors, Senators... and one day, President.
And as we commemorate 163 years since Gettysburg and 250 years of American democracy, the future of our country is again at stake.

As America marked its 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, it is a good time to reflect on the freedom of this great nation as a constitutional republic.
President Trump's America 250 address on July 4th solidified that message. Even after storms delayed the celebration on the National Mall, the crowd returned because America is the nation where the show must go on. The President connected the Declaration, the Constitution, the flags that defined our history, the heroes who defeated fascism and communism, and the future of American greatness through the Artemis astronauts and the next frontier of space.
_**He called America the "home of freedom" and the "land of liberty." He described the moment as "freedom's triumph over tyranny." And he made the contrast clear: "America will never be a communist country." He also said the communist system is "the opposite of the American system."**_
**So how many communist countries are democracies?**
**The answer is simple: none.Connecticut and the Himes Problem**
## Freedom matters directly in Connecticut's 4th District.
Congressman Jim Himes has tried to position himself as a moderate, and he even joined the House vote denouncing the horrors of socialism. That resolution passed 285-98 and stated that socialist ideology has repeatedly collapsed into communist regimes, totalitarian rule, and brutal dictatorships.
But one symbolic vote is not enough - It was probably a Hall Pass.
> The real question is whether Jim Himes will stand up to the radical left inside his own party as it elevates candidates who openly embrace democratic socialism, public ownership, and Marxist language. Zohran Mamdani, for example, calls himself a democratic socialist and has used the phrase "seizing the means of production."
Connecticut does not need a congressman who triangulates after the danger becomes politically obvious. **Connecticut needs a congressman who will say clearly, consistently, and without apology that America 's future is freedom, capitalism, constitutional rights, and opportunity.**
## **The First Step - Exercise Freedom at the Primary**
## The first step is to vote in the Republican Primary on August 11, with early voting from August 3-9.
Primaries are often low turnout, but this year they matter more than ever. If we want to stop the spread of socialism, defeat the radical left, and send a pro-freedom voice to Congress, we cannot wait until November. The work begins now for real momentum in November.
> Remember to Vote in the Republican Primary August 11th with Early Voting August 3-9 - [https://calendar.app.google/XMFRtTU8Zd1Cy2oU6](https://substack.com/redirect/65a09e9d-c078-4bec-a823-f858eac32161?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## **The History Is Clear**
Every communist one-party state promises equality. In practice, it produces dictatorship. China, Cuba, Vietnam, Laos, and North Korea are all rated "Not Free" by Freedom House. China is controlled by the Chinese Communist Party, with no meaningful national elections and no real political opposition. Cuba is a one-party communist state that outlaws political pluralism, bans independent media, suppresses dissent, and restricts basic civil liberties. North Korea remains one of the least free nations on earth.
Communism began in the Soviet Union with Lenin and was followed by Stalin, whose regime starved, imprisoned, and executed millions. When the Soviet Union collapsed, the nations of Eastern Europe that had lived under communist rule threw it off as soon as they had the chance. That tells us something important: people who actually lived under communism rarely vote to keep it.
Russia today is not a communist state, but it is a warning about what happens when power is centralized and opposition is crushed. Vladimir Putin's Russia is rated "Not Free," with manipulated elections, controlled media, subservient courts, and suppression of genuine opposition.
China offers another lesson. The Chinese Communist Party controls politics, speech, religion, media, universities, and civil society. Cuba offers the same lesson. After Fidel Castro's revolution, Cuba became a one-party dictatorship. Many Cubans fled to the United States, where they built vibrant communities and succeeded under freedom, not communism.
Nicaragua is another warning. Daniel Ortega and the Sandinistas came to power promising liberation. Today, Nicaragua is rated "Not Free," with power consolidated under Ortega and his wife, opposition voices arrested or exiled, citizenship stripped from dissidents, and the rule of law collapsed.
All of these systems follow the same pattern. There are no real elections. There is no free press. There is no independent judiciary. Once the ruling party takes power, it does not leave voluntarily. Society divides into two classes: the political elite who live well, and everyone else who is told to sacrifice.
## **Communism Creates Inequality**
