# **Socialist Seattle 's Chinatown district left as "human dumping ground" ahead of World Cup - Protesters rise up **
Residents and business owners in Seattle's Chinatown International District and Little Saigon are protesting socialist Mayor Katie Wilson ahead of today's US-Belgium World Cup match, **[accusing her of neglecting their neighborhoods](https://substack.com/redirect/88942036-70ae-4eb6-a075-a9569f9bf2ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while less than a mile from Lumen Field. Community advocate Gary Lee called Wilson out publicly, accusing her of turning the CID into a "human dumping ground" for homeless individuals and drug users.

* **Wilson 's office acknowledged crime and disorder in the CID had "gone unaddressed for far too long"** and pledged continued work with the community. The mayor did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

subject: Why JD Vance’s story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
What this says about this moment in America | | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

You don’t hire an arsonist to run the fire department.

Linda McMahon’s tenure as Secretary of Education has been an unmitigated disaster for our students. **[That’s why I co-sponsored articles of impeachment to remove her – and why I’m asking you to add your name as a community co-sponsor.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765311/632088165/1866242139?contactdata=qdtUXsjT7jY5rdu9T2/6mVdilNV/61rR5OXxQF+Zbam+e2izV0w5i7YO6p0SIcLOXGoDpP7nAGIxuKqjeAsdmcooWdEfaKs69Ztx3srAMnHtrnv0GYuQ8vC4fouYK4aWNYDqDrsgz8ZiR1bmDAM4ICJDu/q4HoD1euYhws26VKY=&ms=cls-em-petition-20260706-LindaMcMahon-365do&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmM2MTM4ZWMtODk3OS1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhMTRiNmQ2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6u34KTK7j4rB5Ftr99Ac7geE-xyxBZUk4O1mkLjOkAQ=&emci=9bf4d2bb-8979-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=bc6138ec-8979-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=22554739)** [Add your name »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765314/632088168/1866242139?contactdata=qdtUXsjT7jY5rdu9T2/6mVdilNV/61rR5OXxQF+Zbam+e2izV0w5i7YO6p0SIcLOXGoDpP7nAGIxuKqjeAsdmcooWdEfaKs69Ztx3srAMnHtrnv0GYuQ8vC4fouYK4aWNYDqDrsgz8ZiR1bmDAM4ICJDu/q4HoD1euYhws26VKY=&ms=cls-em-petition-20260706-LindaMcMahon-365do&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmM2MTM4ZWMtODk3OS1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhMTRiNmQ2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6u34KTK7j4rB5Ftr99Ac7geE-xyxBZUk4O1mkLjOkAQ=&emci=9bf4d2bb-8979-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=bc6138ec-8979-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=22554739) Secretary McMahon’s track record at the Department of Education demonstrates a reckless disregard for America’s students:
1. **She couldn’t get Congress to abolish the department, so she’s dismantling it piece by piece.** Since taking office, McMahon has quietly relocated the Department’s core responsibilities to six other federal agencies through 14 separate agreements. No votes, no Congressional approval, and certainly no plan to ensure coordinated service in support of our students.
2. **She lied under oath during her Senate confirmation hearing.** When asked, she promised to spend every dollar Congress appropriates for our schools. In reality, she’s unilaterally cancelled contracts and held up funding for programs like migrant education and afterschool programs.
3. **She’s gutted the agency from the inside.** Her own Inspector General confirmed it last month: a 40% cut to staff, and billions of dollars in grants and contracts cancelled – money that should have been funding tutoring, school meals, research, and support for the students who need it most.

**Linda McMahon is not fit to lead the agency responsible for our children’s future. She should be removed from office before she does more damage.**

clean_body: Linda McMahon’s tenure at the Department of Education has been an unmitigated disaster for our students. | = = = | | Hi Friend, You don’t hire an arsonist to run the fire department. You don't put the fox in charge of the henhouse. And you shouldn’t have someone leading the Department of Education who has said, in her own words, that her goal is to eliminate the Department of Education. Linda McMahon’s tenure as Secretary of Education has been an unmitigated disaster for our students. Secretary McMahon’s track record at the Department of Education demonstrates a reckless disregard for America’s students: 1. She couldn’t get Congress to abolish the department, so she’s dismantling it piece by piece. Since taking office, McMahon has quietly relocated the Department’s core responsibilities to six other federal agencies through 14 separate agreements. No votes, no Congressional approval, and certainly no plan to ensure coordinated service in support of our students. 2. She lied under oath during her Senate confirmation hearing. When asked, she promised to spend every dollar Congress appropriates for our schools. In reality, she’s unilaterally cancelled contracts and held up funding for programs like migrant education and afterschool programs. 3. She’s gutted the agency from the inside. Her own Inspector General confirmed it last month: a 40% cut to staff, and billions of dollars in grants and contracts cancelled – money that should have been funding tutoring, school meals, research, and support for the students who need it most. Linda McMahon is not fit to lead the agency responsible for our children’s future. She should be removed from office before she does more damage. body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM4MjMyMzMS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjUwMDA0MTQ0OQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, As many of us have been celebrating the 250th anniversary of America’s founding,
LCV also recognizes that we are at an inflection point in our nation’s history.This country was built on the principles of free and fair elections, checks and
balances, an independent judiciary, and the right to organize. These values
remain central to who we are, and to our mission at LCV. But the Trump administration is attacking these principles, and threatening the
last half a century of progress on both environmental and civil rights issues. In the last 18 months, the Trump administration has: ❌ Gutted the Environmental Protection Agency that helps keep our air and water
clean

❌ Dismantled the Voting Rights Act of 1965, reversing protections against racial
discrimination in voting

❌ Stripped protections for public lands and waters

❌ Attacked the rights of the LGBTQ+ community

❌ ...and so much more. We all want the next 250 years in this country to be better, not worse. LCV
won’t stand by and let the Trump administration take us backwards. Here at LCV, we are envisioning and working toward a future where: ✅ Everyone has access to clean air and clean water

✅ Energy is clean, affordable, and accessible

✅ American democracy is strong

✅ We are able to make meaningful progress in tackling the climate crisis to
ensure a liveable planet for all of us now, and for generations to come. We need you with us. I hope you will join LCV and take action to build a
brighter future. How you can take action right now: Read LCV’s blog post: "America 250: Facing attacks on the American Dream, LCV envisions a brighter future" https://links.messages.lcv. Get involved https://links.messages.lcv. by taking an online action and stay up to date with our advocacyCall your member of Congress https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/x_ and tell them to:Keep public lands in public handsSupport the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore protections for votingSupport the Energy Bills Relief Act to improve access to clean energy and lower energy bills Thank you for standing with LCV to help us build a healthy, prosperous and
equitable America. Together we canprotect people and the planet today, for the next 250 years, and for future
generations. Leah Donahey

body:
I'm just a geologist-turned-brewer who entered public service to do what's right for the people of my state.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765758/632089490/-1473932214?refcode=logo&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDRmNjg5ZC04Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J0wZiVaHAT9zIkWpVS7PEmQ02SAi6RDaHeYitZGSed8=) I'll be honest, folks. I never saw myself serving in the U.S. Senate.

This is a longer email about my story and how I came to fight for hardworking Coloradans in the Senate, and I hope you’ll read it until the end. **[But if you don’t have time, please, take a moment and chip in a couple bucks to my campaign. →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765759/632089491/1973964749?refcode=email_070626_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDRmNjg5ZC04Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J0wZiVaHAT9zIkWpVS7PEmQ02SAi6RDaHeYitZGSed8=)** | | [Donate →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765760/632089492/1973964749?refcode=email_070626_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDRmNjg5ZC04Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J0wZiVaHAT9zIkWpVS7PEmQ02SAi6RDaHeYitZGSed8=)
---
Back in the mid-1980s, I was a geologist — until I wasn’t. Our company got sold and we all got laid off. I used part of my severance to buy an old Chevy convertible, and drove to visit my brother in Berkeley, CA. He showed me one of the first brewpubs in America and I loved it. I came back to Denver and took a gamble, risking every scrap of my savings in opening the Wynkoop Brewing Company in downtown Denver.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765761/632089493/1973964749?refcode=email_070626_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDRmNjg5ZC04Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J0wZiVaHAT9zIkWpVS7PEmQ02SAi6RDaHeYitZGSed8=)
I remember working 80-hour weeks. I remember lying awake at night, wondering how we were going to make it. And I remember being so frustrated that our government was focusing more on decisions that’d help politicians get reelected rather than helping solve our problems.

So I ran for Mayor. To everyone’s surprise, especially mine, I won in a landslide. From then on, I focused every day on making decisions based on what was best for Denver.

I then became the first Denver Mayor in 120 years to be elected Governor, on the premise of uniting people and getting things done. We expanded health care to half a million people and created the first methane regulations in any state or country in the world.

And after we flipped Colorado’s Senate seat in 2020, we worked to deliver real change for Coloradans. We invested billions of dollars to confront the climate crisis, lowered prescription drug costs, made investments to rebuild our infrastructure, and brought thousands of good-paying manufacturing jobs back to America.

Now, we’re in the fight of our lives as Trump’s extreme agenda threatens to undo all that work. We refused to let him auction off our public lands or use your tax dollars to give handouts to felons like Tina Peters.
But look, I’ve also seen how broken Washington is – and how Trump has unleashed corruption like a pandemic. I see politicians who only listen to those who cut big campaign checks while ignoring families trying to afford health care. I’ve seen how Trump operates: money comes in, favors go out.

Here's why I'm telling you this: **what drives our work is the people of Colorado.**

The families who are struggling to maintain their health insurance after Trump gutted the Affordable Care Act to give tax cuts to his friends in the Epstein class. The workers who are working full-time and still need a second job to afford their rent. The kids who are studying science and are already worried that the funding for their research will never come back.
As I said, I never thought I’d find myself in the U.S. Senate, but I’m running for re-election because it’s been the honor of a lifetime to fight for you. And, too much is at stake to stop now.

That’s why I don't take money from corporate PACs like your typical politician. Instead, I rely on grassroots folks like you. And it’s why I'm depending on your contribution today to help us defend Colorado this November. Even just $5 here or $10 there goes a long way in a campaign like ours.
**[So I have to ask: will you make a donation of whatever is meaningful to you? Together, we can defend this seat we flipped back in 2020 and keep power in the hands of Coloradans:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134765762/632089494/1973964749?refcode=email_070626_bio-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDRmNjg5ZC04Yjc5LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J0wZiVaHAT9zIkWpVS7PEmQ02SAi6RDaHeYitZGSed8=)**

Our company got sold and we all got laid off. I used part of my severance to buy an old Chevy convertible, and drove to visit my brother in Berkeley, CA. He showed me one of the first brewpubs in America and I loved it. I came back to Denver and took a gamble, risking every scrap of my savings in opening the Wynkoop Brewing Company in downtown Denver. = I remember working 80-hour weeks. I remember lying awake at night, wondering how we were going to make it. And I remember being so frustrated that our government was focusing more on decisions that’d help politicians get reelected rather than helping solve our problems. So I ran for Mayor. To everyone’s surprise, especially mine, I won in a landslide. From then on, I focused every day on making decisions based on what was best for Denver. I then became the first Denver Mayor in 120 years to be elected Governor, on the premise of uniting people and getting things done. We expanded health care to half a million people and created the first methane regulations in any state or country in the world. And after we flipped Colorado’s Senate seat in 2020, we worked to deliver real change for Coloradans. We invested billions of dollars to confront the climate crisis, lowered prescription drug costs, made investments to rebuild our infrastructure, and brought thousands of good-paying manufacturing jobs back to America. Now, we’re in the fight of our lives as Trump’s extreme agenda threatens to undo all that work. We refused to let him auction off our public lands or use your tax dollars to give handouts to felons like Tina Peters. But look, I’ve also seen how broken Washington is – and how Trump has unleashed corruption like a pandemic. I see politicians who only listen to those who cut big campaign checks while ignoring families trying to afford health care. I’ve seen how Trump operates: money comes in, favors go out. Here's why I'm telling you this: what drives our work is the people of Colorado. The families who are struggling to maintain their health insurance after Trump gutted the Affordable Care Act to give tax cuts to his friends in the Epstein class. The workers who are working full-time and still need a second job to afford their rent. The kids who are studying science and are already worried that the funding for their research will never come back. As I said, I never thought I’d find myself in the U.S. Senate, but I’m running for re-election because it’s been the honor of a lifetime to fight for you. And, too much is at stake to stop now. That’s why I don't take money from corporate PACs like your typical politician. Instead, I rely on grassroots folks like you. And it’s why I'm depending on your contribution today to help us defend Colorado this November. Even just $5 here or $10 there goes a long way in a campaign like ours. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | = | | | = | = | | | = | = Thanks for all your support, John | | Email is a key way for us to stay in touch and make sure you get the latest updates from our campaign. But if you would like to unsubscribe, . Want to hear about our campaign? Where we’re going? How we’re fighting the Trump administration? name: Tim Walz
subject: I didn’t plan on getting involved
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
#
Hi, it’s Gov. Tim Walz.
I've got to tell you, I was a little surprised to wake up and see Georgia's Republican candidate for governor spending his day attacking _**me.**_
I'm up here in Minnesota doing my job. He's down in Georgia running for governor.
_**Wouldn't you think he'd be talking about what he'd do for the people of Georgia?**_
Instead, Rick Jackson is trying to score points with Donald Trump. In fact, he says he wants to be _**"Trump's favorite governor."**_
Well, there you have it.
He's more interested in getting Donald Trump's attention than earning the trust of Georgia families. That's why he's dragging me into his campaign. And it's why he's taking dishonest shots at Keisha Lance Bottoms, too.
Look, I know Keisha. She's tough, she's honest, and she's spent her career fighting for Georgia families—not trying to impress politicians in Washington.
Georgia deserves a governor who's focused on lowering costs, creating opportunity, and making life better for the people who live there—not someone who's auditioning to be Trump's favorite.
**[So I'm asking if you'll help Keisha fight back. Will you split a contribution to her campaign and Small Town PAC today? Your donation helps her build the campaign Georgia deserves and defeat a candidate who's got his priorities all wrong.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-202706-partner-klb.p3-xpE&amount=5&refcode=em20260706-837&t=2&akid=837%2E34582%2Ern-89_)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-202706-partner-klb.p3-xpE&amount=5&refcode=20260706-837&t=21&akid=837%2E34582%2Ern-89_)**
I've always believed public service is about showing up, doing the work, and looking out for your neighbors.
Keisha believes that, too.
Rick Jackson can keep trying to impress Donald Trump. Keisha will keep fighting for Georgia.
I know which one I'd rather have as governor.
Thanks,
Tim Walz

Thanks, Tim Walz Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to build a Democratic Party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America. Together, we're finding and recruiting thoughtful, hardworking people to run for office, and supporting a new generation of leaders who truly reflect and understand their communities.

| | | Peter, **We just finished reading thousands of responses to our latest WFP Supporter Survey.** The overwhelming takeaway was this: **Working people aren't asking for yachts.** We're asking for the basics. To see a doctor without worrying about the bill. To afford a place to call home. To know that if we work hard, we can build a stable life instead of constantly wondering how we're going to make ends meet. In the richest country in the history of the world, that shouldn't be controversial. **But every time working people ask for the basics, we're told we have to "be realistic" while billionaires get another tax break and corporations rake in record profits.** We're done accepting that lie. [**That's why we're building a party that fights for working people. clean_body: | | | Peter, We just finished reading thousands of responses to our latest WFP Supporter Survey. The overwhelming takeaway was this: Working people aren't asking for yachts. We're asking for the basics. To see a doctor without worrying about the bill. To afford a place to call home. To know that if we work hard, we can build a stable life instead of constantly wondering how we're going to make ends meet. In the richest country in the history of the world, that shouldn't be controversial. But every time working people ask for the basics, we're told we have to "be realistic" while billionaires get another tax break and corporations rake in record profits. We're done accepting that lie. When we asked which policies would make the biggest difference for you and your family, nearly 60% of respondents chose guaranteed healthcare — more than any other option. Affordable housing wasn’t far behind, with more than 40% saying that lower rents, mortgages, and utility costs would make the biggest difference in their lives. And just as many people told us they couldn't choose at all, because every one of these priorities — from good union jobs to affordable childcare to paid family leave — are essential for working families. We also asked what they want WFP candidates to fight for. The top priorities were taking on billionaires and corporate power (43%) , guaranteeing healthcare (43%) , protecting democracy and civil rights (42%) , and ending the influence of big money in politics (38%). These are the priorities of people who haven't lowered their expectations — just their tolerance for politicians who refuse to fight for them That's why nearly two-thirds of respondents said they disapprove of the job Democratic leaders in Congress are doing. But frustration isn't the same as hopelessness, Peter. In the very same survey, 74% said they're hopeful about our movement's ability to build working-class power and stand up to the far right. We think that's because people are seeing that fighting for working people isn't the political risk they've been told it is — it's how we win. Across the country, we're recruiting and electing Working Families champions at every level of government, from school boards and city halls to state legislatures and Congress. We're growing our progressive bloc in Washington, and we've been on a winning streak because election after election, voters are choosing candidates who are willing to fight for working people. Now we have four months until November's general election to build on that momentum. In solidarity, WFP Digital Team Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. name: Voter Action Project
subject: Changes that harm mail-in voting
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=070626_3&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list -- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote.
Team, Every voter needs to know about these massive changes. Will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about the new USPS rules so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=070626_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=070626_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=070626_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=070626_3&amount=50]

We're worried about every mail-in voter getting their ballot in on time, but especially those most vulnerable to these changes, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home. None of them deserve to be disenfranchised from our elections over DOGE's cost-cutting measures or Trump's conspiracies about mail-in ballots.
Whether you can fuel our work today or not, we appreciate your support and we hope you can spread the word about these USPS changes to your friends, family, and colleagues. You never know how a quick mention of something like this news might truly impact someone else's life.
Thank you,
The Voter Action Project Team

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

body:

# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260706-3002)
Peter,
On Sunday, new polling for the Wisconsin governor's race dropped. It shows Fran leading the pack, and beating Tom Tiffany head-to-head.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/15602?t=1&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz)
And it's not a one-off. It's the latest in a string of polls showing Fran at the front of this race. Fran has consistently led Marquette Law School Poll, the gold standard of Wisconsin polling.
[**Fran can win in November. But first, we need to make it through the August 11th primary. And we can't do that without your support.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260706.D8FCv7&refcode=em20260706-3002&t=2&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz)
Last week, we shared Fran's [New York Times](https://act.francescahong.com/go/15598?t=3&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz) feature with you. The coverage hasn't stopped:
[John Nichols of The Nation put Fran in the tradition of Fighting Bob La Follette](https://act.francescahong.com/go/15599?t=4&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz), reminding us that “Wisconsin is a maverick state that is quite capable of upending status quo thinking about what is possible in our politics.”
[The Intercept profiled the volunteer movement powering campaigns like ours](https://act.francescahong.com/go/15600?t=5&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz), called Fran a "formidable DSA candidate for governor," and quoted our campaign’s true definition of socialism: “Taking care of our neighbors, taking care of people’s economic needs.”
[The Wisconsin Examiner spent a day with Fran](https://act.francescahong.com/go/15601?t=6&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz) as she campaigned in Tom Tiffany's backyard and found common ground with voters on property taxes, public schools, and protecting the environment.
The pundits keep asking whether a democratic socialist can win in the Midwest. Wisconsin answered that a century ago. Milwaukee elected democratic socialists for fifty years, and they fixed the sewers, built public infrastructure and balanced the budgets. They governed for working people. That's a Wisconsin legacy to be proud of, and it's the future Wisconsin deserves.
But headlines and history lessons don't win elections. Organizing does. We're 36 days out from the primary, and we’re up against candidates with establishment money and establishment backing.
[We've set a goal of raising **$250,000 before the August 11 primary** , and we’re counting on your support, because Fran doesn't take any corporate PAC money.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260706.D8FCv7&refcode=em20260706-3002&t=7&akid=3002%2E105371%2EWb-2Tz)
Can a democratic socialist win in Wisconsin? You betcha.

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=429%2E127862%2Eks079t)
Folks, I need to show you something.
Here's what Nevada voter registration looks like right now:
**_Active Registered Voters in Nevada_**
🔵 Democrats: 574,128
🔴 Republicans: 577,737
Difference: **-3,609**
The math isn’t exactly on our side, but there’s one variable missing: **non-partisan voters. 787,873 Nevada voters fit into that category.**
**In a race this close, these voters will have a major impact in determining who wins.**
Every dollar we raise goes toward reaching these folks _and_ mobilizing our Democratic base to get out and vote come election season.
We have a message that resonates across the state — one focused on lowering costs and holding powerful interests accountable. Now, we just need the resources to broadcast it across the state.
**[Please, chip in $5 today to help us reach as many voters as possible.](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260706_2_ak.5wwJn3&amount=5&refcode=em20260706-422&t=3&akid=429%2E127862%2Eks079t)**

Thank you,
Aaron

body:
There’s a reason this story mattered to Charlie| | | |
---
| | | Friend,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**
---

Friend, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

Hi Peter,
This past holiday weekend, thousands of Oregonians headed into the forests we love most, pitching tents beneath towering trees, hiking familiar trails, cooling off beside mountain streams, and making memories in the public lands that belong to all of us.
But while we celebrate these places, they’re facing some of the biggest threats we’ve seen in generations.
From Mount Hood National Forest to the Columbia River Gorge, nearly 2 million acres of Oregon’s forests are at risk if the Trump administration moves forward with plans to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule: one of the strongest protections our national forests have ever had ( read more [https://morethanjustparks.substack.com/p/trump-admin-targets-five-of-oregons?utm_source=post-email-title&publication_id=1594349&post_id=195273529&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=5ksrax&triedRedirect=true] ).
The Roadless Rule protects these wild places from industrial logging and road construction, preserving clean water, wildlife habitat, and the forests that communities across Oregon depend on. Oregonians have made their voices clear: when the Roadless Rule was opened for public comment, more than 99% of comments opposed the administration’s plan to eliminate these protections.
But now, instead of listening to the public, Senate Republicans are trying to repeal the Roadless Rule through Congress.
Senator Mike Lee has been one of the leading voices behind efforts to roll back conservation protections under Trump 2.0, putting our public lands at risk for the benefit of corporate polluters and logging interests.
Meanwhile, Oregon Congresswoman Andrea Salinas is fighting back with the Roadless Area Conservation Act (RACA), legislation that would permanently protect these treasured landscapes. OLCV and LCV are proud to support her work, but defending Oregon’s forests requires a strong grassroots movement behind it.
These forests aren’t just lines on a map. They’re the places where we go to reconnect, recharge, and remember why Oregon is worth protecting.
This summer, while you’re gathering outside to enjoy the beauty of Oregon’s public lands, I hope you’re reminded that these places belong to all of us. It’s up to all of us to defend them and protect them for generations to come.
Will you give a generous gift to OLCV today to power our work defending Oregon’s forests, holding decision-makers accountable, and protecting the places that make our state special? [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2]
Protect Oregon's Forests [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2?am=20&amtOpts=&recurringAm=20&recurringAmtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=Gk3lrlwYpQE3dJScDjTTUk1p6H5RVKfkt6X2peE7hKgPjLlbKgCyi23dk36Dvm8HosFZJAPD98Z2LrSrZKyKovF3FkaPDbnUetXfzfUodVqw4xvkAejNduAw3X8IOa0t]
The fight to protect our forests won’t happen without people like you standing up.
Thank you for helping protect Oregon’s forests today and for generations to come.
